headline: Energy's stale marks finally caught down 4-5% while crude stabilized — and the credit/vol composite halved again to -54, so the rotation is now de-risking, not reallocation.
summary: The gap I flagged yesterday closed violently. Energy equity had been marked as of 10/30 and contained none of the Brent collapse; today XLE printed -4.0%, XOP -5.0%, OIH -5.5%, XOM -4.0%, CVX -3.3%. The catch-down happened on the day crude itself stopped falling: WTI +0.8% to 97.27 and Brent +0.4% to 105.14 as headlines around the US strike on Qeshm Island fought the Iran de-escalation trade. That is the wrong sequence for energy longs — equities repriced the move after the commodity had already stopped going down. And the air isn't out: XLE is still +7.1% on the month and 15.3% above its 200-day at the 90th percentile, XOP +4.7% and 13.8% extended, XOM and CVX 16.8% and 18.8% above their 200-days at the 90th percentile. Brent is -7.7% on the week. The marks and the barrel still disagree.

The bigger change is underneath. The credit & vol composite went from -27 to -54 in a session while the risk regime slipped to -17 from -15. HYG fell 0.7% and HYG/IEF is -2.7% on the month at z=-1.94 and rolling over, sitting at the 31st percentile of its year; LQD -0.5%. VIX is 21.29, +39.1% on the month (z=1.53), VIX3M 21.60, and the VIX/VIX3M term structure prints 0.979 at z=1.72 and turning up — effectively flat, one bad tape from inversion, with SKEW at 152.78. For six sessions the equity index has drifted (SPX -0.5%, -2.3% on the month) while the hedging complex and junk have gone the other way. Credit is no longer merely refusing to confirm; it is actively dissenting. Midterm results tonight and AMD's print are the two obvious catalysts into that setup.

The dispersion inside the index is now historic. RSP/SPY is +1.2% on the day and +7.3% on the month at z=3.68 with acceleration z=4.0 — up from 3.00/3.55 yesterday, the most extreme reading on the board and getting more extreme. Read it correctly: equal-weight at the 95th percentile against NDX -9.1% on the month and QQQ/SPY at z=-2.84 with acceleration -3.30 is mega-cap liquidation, not health. Semis are the epicentre and the selling accelerated — SOXX -3.8% to -23.0% on the month (z=-2.57), SMH -19.4%, AMD -7.5% and -26.4%, MU -5.8% and -22.4%, ORCL -8.8% and -38.0% year-to-date at the 3rd percentile of its range. It is global: KOSPI -3.6% (-19.3% on the month), TAIEX -3.6%, EWY -21.0% on the month, USDKRW +1.4%. Momentum is being torched — MTUM -14.8% on the month at z=-2.79, high-beta/low-vol -20.4% at z=-3.19, growth/value at the 0th percentile of its year. That is a market-structure risk, not a style rotation.

The bid is going to houses, shelves and balance sheets. ITB +4.6% and XHB +3.6% on the day, DHI +4.7%, HD +3.6% (z=2.89, acceleration 3.20), with XHB/SPY +4.1% and +10.7% on the month — housing is trading the 37bp monthly rally in the 10-year to 4.91 and 35bp in the 30-year to 5.28, not the 30-year mortgage at 7.24, which is still +21bp on the month. Financials joined: XLF +1.9%, KRE +2.4%, KBE +2.3%, KIE +9.5% on the month at z=1.92, all with relative strength turning up despite 2s10s flattening to 32bp at the 22nd percentile. The defensives are now stretched to the point of being a risk themselves: XLP at the 100th percentile, +12.8% on the month at z=3.37; SPLV at the 99th percentile; XLV +11.1% at z=2.65; LMT +27.3% at z=3.53. Meanwhile the deflation trade re-accelerated in metals after a one-day pause — silver -2.7% (-17.7% on the month, 3rd percentile), platinum -1.6% at the 0th percentile, copper -2.4%, gold/silver +1.6% to 79.55 at z=2.18 with acceleration 1.35. The whole AI-power-and-materials chain is in liquidation: uranium -17.2% on the month, rare earths -20.5%, lithium -13.3%, GRID -10.2%, NLR -12.7% at the 0th percentile.

good.text: Breadth keeps widening at a record clip: RSP/SPY +1.2% on the day, +7.3% on the month, z=3.68 with acceleration 4.0; equal-weight S&P +4.9% on the month at the 95th percentile. Transports confirm — DJT +1.5%, IYT/SPY +2.3% and +6.0% on the month.

The long end keeps easing: 10-year -37bp on the month to 4.91, 5-year -36bp to 4.70, 30-year -35bp to 5.28, each at a 1-month move z-score below -1.4. TLT +5.5% on the month. That is the fuel for the housing bid.

Housing and retail broke out hard — ITB +4.6% (+11.9% on the month), XHB +3.6%, DHI +4.7%, HD +3.6% at z=2.89 with acceleration 3.20, XRT +2.1% with XRT/SPY at z=2.45. Consumer discretionary +2.4% on the day and relative strength turning up.

Financials are taking leadership from tech: XLF +1.9% (+7.6% on the month, 93rd percentile, relative strength +10.1% and turning up), KRE +2.4%, KBE +2.3%, KRE/SPY z=0.92, insurance +9.5% on the month at z=1.92, JPM +1.1%.

Disinflation is still transmitting: 5-year breakevens -7bp to 2.39, 10-year -5bp to 2.29 at the 34th percentile, gasoline -11.1% on the month (z=-1.11). Grains are rolling too — corn -10.4%, wheat -11.6% on the month.
Plumbing is a tailwind at the margin: the TGA drained 8.5% in a day to $951.6bn, and EM FX held — CEW +0.5%, USD/MXN -1.2%, USD/CNY -0.7% on the month at the 0th percentile of its range.

bad.text: Credit and vol composite collapsed from -27 to -54. HYG -0.7% with HYG/IEF -2.7% on the month at z=-1.94 and rolling over; VIX 21.29 and +39.1% on the month; VIX/VIX3M at 0.979, z=1.72 and turning up — the term structure is one session from inverting with SKEW at 152.78.

The semiconductor sell-off is accelerating, not exhausting: SOXX -3.8% to -23.0% on the month (z=-2.57, acceleration -2.85), AMD -7.5% into tonight's print and -26.4% on the month, MU -5.8%/-22.4%, ORCL -8.8% and -38.0% YTD at the 3rd percentile, SMH/SPY z=-2.93.

Momentum unwind is a market-structure event: MTUM -14.8% on the month (z=-2.79), high-beta/low-vol -20.4% (z=-3.19, acceleration -3.48), growth/value -12.1% and at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range. Crowded-trade liquidation, not rotation.

The front end still won't play along: 3-month bill 4.21 at the 89th percentile, 2-year 4.59, 2s10s down to 32bp (22nd percentile), 3m10y -39bp on the month to 70bp, 10-year real yield 2.62 and +69bp YTD, 30-year mortgage 7.24 and +21bp on the month. Flattening on falling breakevens is demand loss, not relief.

Hard-asset liquidation resumed after a one-day pause: silver -2.7% (-17.7% on the month, 3rd percentile), platinum -1.6% at the 0th percentile, copper -2.4%, gold -1.1%, gold/silver +1.6% to 79.55 at z=2.18 with acceleration 1.35. The AI-power complex is in freefall — uranium -17.2%, rare earths -20.5%, lithium -13.3%, NLR -12.7% on the month.

EM is fracturing by country: Bovespa -18.1% on the week, EWZ -15.8% on the month (z=-2.16) with USD/BRL +5.1% and turning up, USD/KRW +1.4% on the day, EEM/SPY -7.6% on the month at the 16th percentile.

trades.name: Short HYG — credit catches down to vol
trades.line: Short HYG / buy Dec puts: credit dissent vs a 0.98 VIX term structure
trades.expr: Short HYG outright, or buy Dec 76 puts; finance by selling equivalent-delta IEF upside if you want it duration-neutral (the HYG/IEF ratio is the cleaner expression).
trades.thesis: Credit is the only part of the board that has refused to confirm every equity bounce since September, and today the credit & vol composite halved again to -54. With the VIX term structure at 0.979 and turning up, junk at the 31st percentile of its year is not priced for a vol event.
trades.trigger: HYG -0.7% on the day with HYG/IEF -2.7% on the month at z=-1.94 and rolling over, while VIX rose to 21.29 (+39.1% on the month) and SKEW sits at 152.78.
trades.stop: HYG/IEF reclaims its 200-day (currently -0.23% below) and VIX/VIX3M drops back under 0.94; or a post-midterm risk melt-up that takes SPX back above its 1-month high.
trades.target: HYG toward 75 / HYG-IEF ratio down another 2-3%, roughly a 1.5-2x payoff on the put structure.

trades.name: Short XOP — the energy mark is still stale
trades.line: Short XOP: still +4.7% on month, 13.8% over 200d, Brent -7.7% on week
trades.expr: Short XOP outright, or buy Dec XOP puts. For the lower-beta version, short XLE against long XOM (XOM is the better balance sheet in a sub-100 WTI world).
trades.thesis: Today's 5% drop was the first instalment of the catch-down, not the whole bill. E&P equity still carries a mid-100s Brent risk premium that the curve has already deleted, and crude's bounce today was a geopolitical headline, not demand.
trades.trigger: XOP -5.0%, OIH -5.5%, XLE -4.0% on the day yet XOP remains +4.7% on the month and 13.8% above its 200-day at the 86th percentile, with Brent -7.7% on the week and WTI only +0.8% today.
trades.stop: Brent closes back above 112 (re-escalation premium) or XOP holds +5% above its 200-day for a week.
trades.target: XOP back to its 200-day, roughly 12% lower; OIH is already rolling over as the lead indicator.

trades.name: Long ITB — duration rally in equity form
trades.line: Long ITB: +4.6% today, +11.9% on month, 10y -37bp on the month
trades.expr: Long ITB (or XHB for broader supply-chain beta); express leveraged via Jan ITB 100/115 call spreads. Pair hedge: short a half-weight of XLU, which is rolling over at z=1.86 after a 9.6% monthly run.
trades.thesis: The 37bp monthly drop in the 10-year is finally reaching the most rate-sensitive equity cohort, and housing has the rare combination of improving relative strength and a depressed starting point — XHB/SPY is still at the 32nd percentile of its 52-week range, so this is early, not chased.
trades.trigger: ITB +4.6% and XHB +3.6% on the day; XHB/SPY +4.1% on the day and +10.7% on the month at z=1.99; DHI +4.7%, HD +3.6% with acceleration z=3.20; mortgage rate -8bp on the week.
trades.stop: The 30-year mortgage rate pushing above its recent high (7.24 and rising) or 10-year yield back above 5.10; ITB losing its 200-day (1.9% below current price).
trades.target: XHB/SPY to the 50th percentile of its range, roughly another 8-10% of relative gain; ITB 108-110.

trades.name: Long XLF / short XLK
trades.line: Long XLF vs short XLK: leadership handoff, +10.1% vs -10.8% RS
trades.expr: Dollar-neutral: long XLF, short XLK. Add KRE as a third of the long leg for the steepener optionality.
trades.thesis: Tech is losing leadership while financials gain it, and the financial complex is broad — banks, regionals, insurance and brokers all turned up together. XLK's relative strength is rolling over from an extreme; XLF's is turning up from a base at the 93rd percentile of price.
trades.trigger: XLF +1.9% vs XLK -2.9% on the day; XLF relative strength +10.1% on the month and turning up vs XLK -10.8% and rolling over; KRE +2.4%, KBE +2.3%, KIE +9.5% on the month at z=1.92.
trades.stop: 2s10s flattening through 15bp (the funding-margin kill) or XLF relative strength rolling back over; a decisive AMD/semis-led tech reversal that puts SMH/SPY back above its 200-day.
trades.target: Another 8% on the pair; XLF relative strength to match its 2024 leadership extremes.

trades.name: Long EWW / short EWZ
trades.line: Long Mexico vs short Brazil: MXN -1.2% vs BRL stress, z=1.47
trades.expr: Long EWW, short EWZ, equal dollars. For the pure macro version, long MXN / short BRL in the forwards.
trades.thesis: LatAm has split cleanly. Mexico has a firming currency, an index at the 82nd percentile and relative strength turning up; Brazil has a currency breaking out at a 1-month z of 1.47, an equity index down 18.1% in a week and an ETF at z=-2.16. Trade the divergence, not the region.
trades.trigger: USD/MXN -1.2% on the day with MXX +8.7% on the month (z=1.87) and EWW +1.9%; versus USD/BRL +0.9% on the day, +5.1% on the month and turning up, with EWZ -15.8% on the month and BVSP -18.1% on the week.
trades.stop: USD/BRL back under 5.25 (stress unwind) or USD/MXN above 19.20 (Mexico-specific shock).
trades.target: 10-12% on the pair over the quarter.

trades.name: Long volatility into the midterm/AMD window
trades.line: Buy Dec SPY put spread: VIX term structure 0.979, z=1.72, turning up
trades.expr: Buy Dec SPY 740/700 put spreads, or a VIX Dec 24/32 call spread. Size small — this is event insurance, not a core short.
trades.thesis: The index is down only 2.3% on the month while the internals have had a three-sigma dislocation; the gap between a quiet headline tape and a violent rotation underneath is exactly what a flattening-to-inverting term structure prices. Election night and AMD's print are the two detonators.
trades.trigger: VIX/VIX3M at 0.979 (+15.2% on the month, z=1.72, turning up), SKEW 152.78, QQQ/SPY at z=-2.84 with acceleration -3.30, AMD -7.5% on the day into earnings, high-beta/low-vol at z=-3.19.
trades.stop: VIX/VIX3M back below 0.92 and VIX under 18; or SPX reclaiming its 1-month high — cut the structure.
trades.target: VIX into the high 20s / SPX test of its 200-day, roughly 3% below spot; 2-3x on the spread.

trades.name: Long IGV / short SMH
trades.line: Software over semis: IGV/SMH +16.6% on month, z=2.38, turning up
trades.expr: Long IGV, short SMH, dollar-neutral. Trim the short into any SOXX washout below its 1-month low.
trades.thesis: The capex trade is unwinding into the monetisation trade. Semis carry the whole AI build-out risk — Korea, Taiwan and the memory names are all breaking — while software's relative strength has already turned up off a 37th-percentile base.
trades.trigger: IGV/SMH +16.6% on the month at z=2.38 with acceleration 2.30 and turning up; SOXX -23.0% on the month (z=-2.57) versus IGV relative strength +5.1% on 3 months and turning up; KOSPI -3.6% and TAIEX -3.6% overnight.
trades.stop: IGV/SMH back below its 200-day (9.2% lower) or a blowout AMD guide that restores semis leadership.
trades.target: Another 10% on the ratio toward the 60th percentile of its range.
